purpose: DECISIVE TEST — the GitHub writer is UTF-8 text only, so raster bytes cannot be committed directly. Two workarounds are tested in ONE round trip: (A) base64-encode the image into a text file, (B) hand back the image URL as text and let us download it. BOTH must be attempted for every request. We are not accepting a vector-only outcome.

delivery_contract.rule: Attempt BOTH channel A and channel B for every request. Reporting one does not excuse skipping the other. Partial success is valuable; silence is not.

channel_a_base64.what: Write the raw bytes of the GENERATED raster image, base64-encoded, as a UTF-8 text file.
channel_a_base64.format: standard base64 of the raw image bytes. Line breaks every 76 chars are fine. NO data: URI prefix, NO markdown fences, NO quotes, NO JSON wrapper — the file contains ONLY the base64 payload.
channel_a_base64.field: report the path in the result's "files" array

channel_b_url.what: Whatever URL your image tool produced for the generated image — the direct asset link, sandbox path, or file id.
channel_b_url.field: report it in the result's "urls" array (array of strings), and put any auth/expiry caveat in "notes"
channel_b_url.why: Even a short-lived URL is useful: our render job runs same-day and can download it. Give us the URL even if you believe it will expire, and say when you think it expires.

requests.prompt: A photorealistic close-up of a single ripe orange resting on a black reflective surface, dramatic side lighting, shallow depth of field.
requests.notes: This MUST be a real generated raster image from your image tool — NOT hand-written SVG or vector code. Vector is already proven and is not what this test measures. Attempt channel A AND channel B.

diagnostics_required.instruction: If either channel fails, the manifest MUST name the exact step that blocked it. Vague failure notes make this test worthless.
steps_to_report_on: generate — could your image tool produce the image at all?
access — could you read/see the resulting file or its bytes from the same task context?
encode — could you base64-encode those bytes?
write — could you commit the encoded text file to the branch?
url — did the image tool expose any URL, path, or file id, and what is it?
diagnostics_required.note: Report per-step: worked / failed / not-attempted, with one line of why. A precise 'access failed: the image tool output is not visible to the file writer' is a SUCCESSFUL test result. 'Unsupported' with no step named is a FAILED one.
